one_month_reasoning: Window 2026-10-23 to 2026-11-22. No AT&T earnings and no ex-dividend date in the window (dividend declared $0.2775/qtr; next ex-date expected around early January). Scheduled: Verizon Q3 results (Oct 26 per TIKR) and T-Mobile Q3 (Oct 28) - the read-across on postpaid churn and promotions; possible confirmation or denial of the Bloomberg-reported SpaceX talks for ~80,000 cell sites; FCC process on SpaceX's 800 MHz purchase (needs approval) and on the waiver AT&T and Verizon oppose. The stock fell 16.8% in the month to Oct 23 on three news days and sits ~5% above its 52-week low ($19.89); short-term reversal after sharp drops argues for a slight bounce, but the SpaceX news flow is ongoing and two-sided. I stay near-symmetric around $21 with ~9.5% monthly sigma (a bit above the usual 30%/3.5 = 8.6% given event volatility) and a slightly fatter left tail.

thesis_break_reason: At $16 the stock would trade at ~5.3x my NTM horizon EBITDA and ~5.8x NTM EPS, a level that would only make sense if the cash-flow path broke rather than the multiple: e.g. a cut to the $19B+ 2027 FCF guide or the $24B+ buyback plan, a rating downgrade forcing deleveraging ahead of buybacks, or evidence (pricing moves, churn spike) that Starlink Mobile/Verizon have started a wireless price war before 2028.

reverse_dcf_check: 6.0x NTM EBITDA (~$50.2B) is EV ~$301B against unlevered FCF of ~$25B (EBITDA - $22.9B capital investment - ~$2B cash taxes), an ~8.4% unlevered FCF yield; at a ~7% cost of capital that implies roughly -1% a year perpetual decline in real unlevered cash flow after 2028, i.e. EBITDA growth of ~0-1% with capital intensity near 45% of EBITDA - plausible given Starlink Mobile, legacy losses and fiber ARPU pressure, and below management's 5%+ 2028 EBITDA growth.

sbc_treatment.note: FY2025 SBC $536M (10-K, F43), 0.43% of revenue. AT&T's adjusted EPS/EBITDA do not add SBC back, so it is a cost in EBIT, EPS and FCF; share count falls only by net buybacks (stock-plan issuance ~20M a year netted in the horizon count). Peers (VZ, TMUS, CMCSA) on the same GAAP-cost basis.

reasoning: Skeptic lane. Three October drops were traced to primary or near-primary sources: Oct 9 (-10.8% per Yahoo closes; Trefis 9.8%): SpaceX's Oct 8 agreement to buy Grain's nationwide 800 MHz licences for Starlink Mobile (FCC approval needed; ~$8B reported estimate), plus a Scotiabank target cut - a multiple event for a threat that lands in 2028+. Oct 21 (-6.4%): Q3 beat and EPS raise, but postpaid phone adds 379k (vs 432k in Q2), churn 0.92% (vs 0.86% in Q2), fiber ARPU -4% and guided down again for Q4, a Q4 EBITDA hit (acquisition costs + ~$100M vendor settlements), leverage 3.13x with the 2.5x target pushed to 2029 and ~$800M separation cash in 2027 - a small earnings-path cut plus multiple. Oct 23 (-8.0%): Bloomberg-reported SpaceX talks for ~80,000 cell sites (TMUS -7.7%) and target cuts (JPMorgan 33->31, Barclays 24->21) after Bernstein's Oct 12 downgrade to Market Perform - multiple. Q3 GAAP EPS $0.12/$0.13 is depressed by a $2.6B non-cash Mexico impairment ($0.41) and separation charges ($0.09); adjusted $0.65. Credit: net debt $149.8B, Fitch BBB+ negative, Moody's Baa2 (tolerance 3.5x within two years of the EchoStar close), collateral triggers in the 10-Q; no insider buying or selling reported (GuruFocus), short interest small (~118M shares in March 2026). Driver build (6 drivers, 85% of revenue driven): wireless service growth ~2.5% in 2027 and ~1.4% in 2028, internet revenue +13%/+10% with revenue per connection falling, AC EBIT margin to 26.2%, capital investment $22.9B; EBITDA ~$49.2B ex-Mexico in 2027 and ~$50.4B in 2028 (+2.3%, well below the 5%+ guide); EPS $2.56/$2.81 (consensus $2.59 for 2027; management floor ~$2.82 for 2028); FCF $19.0B in 2027 at the guide floor despite a record of ~4% beats, because of separation cash, Mexico and interest. Valuation at the horizon: 6.0x NTM EBITDA (peer trailing median 5.6x, VZ 7.3x, AT&T ~6.3x today), 8.0x NTM EPS (peer median 7.5x, VZ 8.7x), 12% FCF yield; net debt falls to ~$143B and shares to ~6,390M (-5%), so even with a ~0.3x de-rating the research target (12m) is ~$22.8. Weighing honestly: the bear case is about the multiple and post-2027 wireless pricing, not near-term cash flow, and ~12% FCF yield with 5% buybacks cushions the downside. Ladder: median ~$22 (between spot $20.93 and the research target, since momentum is negative and the SpaceX overhang may persist), lognormal-like spread with sigma ~0.27 (realized vol 30%) and a fatter left tail for leverage/price-war risk; bear 25% at $17.2, base 50% at $22.8, bull 25% at $27.9 (engine scenario values). Research was limited by exhausted Bigdata credits (no NTM EBITDA consensus); sell-side notes were read only through press summaries. Not driver-linked: Legacy, Latin America, AC Other and Corporate segments, and the fiber JV adjustment.

drivers.label: Average postpaid phone subscribers
drivers.source: Base: filing (Q4 2025 EX-99.2 postpaid phones 74,214 at 2025-12-31 and 72,749 at 2024-12-31; average 73,482). Path: estimate.
drivers.derivation: 2026: end-2025 74,214 + 9M26 net adds 1,105 (Q3 EX-99.2: Sep-26 base 75,283) + Q4 ~300 = ~75,580; average (74,214+75,580)/2 = 74,897. 2027 net adds ~0.8M (vs 1.55M FY25, 1.1M 9M26) as promotional competition persists -> end 76,380, avg 75,980. 2028 net adds ~0.5M as Starlink Mobile launches (target end-2027) -> end 76,880, avg 76,630.
drivers.guidance_check: AT&T does not guide subscriber adds; see AC service revenue entry in guidance_check.
drivers.why: Volume driver of wireless service revenue (about 54% of revenue). Skeptic path: slower adds than 2025-26 as Verizon chases share and SpaceX enters.
drivers.variant_view: Street/management reading: ~1.2-1.5M adds a year continue on convergence (42.8% of fiber homes take AT&T wireless); +0.5M avg subs adds ~$0.5B revenue, ~$0.08/share at 6x.

drivers.label: AC wireless service revenue per average postpaid phone, per month
drivers.source: Base: filing (Mobility service revenue FY2025 $67,384M = AC wireless service, Q4 2025 EX-99.2 and Q3 2026 EX-99.2 9M25 50,430) / 73,482 avg postpaid phones / 12. Path: estimate.
drivers.derivation: Blended metric (includes prepaid, connected devices and business wireless in the numerator). 2026: AC wireless service 9M 52,118 + Q4 ~17,850 = 69,968 / 74,897 / 12 = $77.85 (+1.9%). 2027 +1.0% (pricing actions annualise, but promotions 'remain the same' per CFO and price locks) = $78.63; 2028 +0.5% = $79.02 as a fourth facilities-based carrier launches.
drivers.guidance_check: Management guides AC service revenue mid-single-digit growth; our wireless service growth (+2.5% 2027) sits below it; see guidance_check.
drivers.why: Price driver; postpaid phone ARPU grew 4% y/y in Q3 26 on rate plans, but Q4 25 ARPU was -0.3% and churn rose; skeptic keeps it near inflation-minus.
drivers.variant_view: If 2025-26 pricing power persists (+2.5%/yr), 2028 wireless service is ~$2.3B higher, worth ~$1.6/share at 6x EBITDA with ~70% flow-through.

drivers.label: Average internet connections (AT&T Fiber, Business Fiber, Internet Air, Business FWA)

drivers.derivation: 2026: Sep-26 16,248 incl. ~1.12M acquired Lumen fiber customers (Feb-2026) + Q4 ~650 net adds = 16,900 at Dec-26; quarterly trapezoid average 15,388. 2027 net adds 2.4M (2026 organic ~2.65M) -> Dec-27 19,300, avg ~18,100. 2028 net adds 2.2M -> avg 20,400.
drivers.guidance_check: No connection guidance; fiber target 40M+ locations by end-2026, 60M+ by 2030 (Q3 26 release).
drivers.why: Volume driver of the growth engine (home internet +23% y/y).
drivers.variant_view: Faster FWA ramp (+0.5M/yr) adds ~$0.6B revenue by 2028.

drivers.label: Internet revenue (AHI + business fiber & advanced connectivity) per average connection, per month
drivers.source: Base: FY2025 internet revenue $16,641M (9M25 filing 6,908 + 5,356; Q4 25 estimated 2,495 + 1,882) / 12,027.5 / 12. Path: estimate.
drivers.derivation: 2026: AHI 9M 8,700 + Q4 ~3,050 and business fiber 9M 5,820 + Q4 ~2,000 = 19,570 / 15,388 / 12 = $105.98 (-8%: lower-ARPU Lumen Quantum base, FWA mix, fiber ARPU -4% y/y in Q3 and guided similar in Q4). 2027 -4% ($101.7), 2028 -2.5% ($99.2) as FWA keeps rising in mix and convergence discounts continue.

model_inputs.structure_note: Driver-led set (run addendum: treat T as held). Six drivers: postpaid phones x blended wireless ARPU (AC Wireless, incl. equipment at a fixed 1.339 ratio), internet connections x revenue per connection (AC Internet), AC EBIT margin (applied to all three AC parts), capital investment. Driven share of FY2025 revenue = (90,230 + 16,641) / 125,648 = 85%. Legacy, Latin America (sold, close Q1 2027), AC Other and Corporate stay plain segments (not driver-linked). Value is carried by EV/EBITDA (0.45), P/E on my own NTM adjusted EPS (0.35) and levered FCF yield (0.20) at the horizon; no DCF leg (policy). Net debt is the company definition at 2026-09-30 (149,819 incl. Mexico held-for-sale finance leases); minorities are the subsidiary preferred interests / NCI on the balance sheet (15,979 + 2,006 redeemable); preferred = Series A 48,000 x $25,000 + Series C 70,000 x $25,000.
model_inputs.gap_note: Judgment calls for Kilian: (1) FY2025 segment bases need Q4 2025 estimates because the new segments start in Q1 2026 and only 9M25 is recast (Q4 25 AHI ~2,495, business fiber ~1,882, legacy ~1,950, AC equipment ~7,577). (2) AC EBIT margin is applied to equipment-heavy wireless and internet alike. (3) NTM EPS ($2.76) and FCF/share ($2.88) for the P/E and FCF legs are my own figures from this build (interest ~$8.0-8.2B, adjusted other income ~$1.9-2.0B, NCI income ~$1.5B, preferred $0.14B, tax 22%), not consensus. (4) Pension/OPEB obligation ($8.1B, 10-Q balance sheet) is not deducted, consistent with peers' EV; deducting it after tax would cost ~$0.95/share. (5) Forward EV/EBITDA peers are trailing filing multiples (no NTM EBITDA consensus available this run). (6) Fiber JV proceeds undisclosed; carried as a $4.0B adjustment.
